newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes pinned back, contango supports.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes pinned back, contango supports.

text.p: A handful of unsold North Sea crude cargoes loading in June and evidence of rising supply next month were keeping spot markets pinned back in early talk on Monday.

Traders said the prompt contango on the Brent paper market was encouraging some refineries to put more crude into storage, lending some support to the market, but fatter North Sea July loading programmes and unsold June barrels kept buyers relaxed.
"We're not expecting much change. The contango and the margins will help but on the other side there are plenty of barrels, including a few June stragglers," said a trader.
Although expected, an increase in July loadings from the Brent and Oseberg streams as fields come out of maintenance would continue to give buyers' the upper hand.

Aug Brent crude dipped a cent to $17.75 a barrel by 1154 GMT on the IPE but intermonth spreads looked a shade softer, Aug/Sept talking at -22/-18 cents, down from -18/-16 cents in late U.S. dealing on Friday.
Brent CFDs for the balance of this week also slipped a couple of cents to talk at Aug Brent -62/-58 cents although activity was thin.

Two July 1-3 cargoes were expected to be nominated from the paper chains on Monday but there were still a couple of June cargoes available despite talk that a U.S. refiner was taking a VLCC trans-Atlantic in the third decade of the month.
The U.S. refiner kept one of two June 28-30 Brent cargoes turning wet on Friday and bought a June 27-29 loader from a Wall Street trader at a Dated-related price.
Texaco Rotterdam late last week restored crude runs at its part of the 420,000 barrels per day (bpd) joint venture Nerefco refinery to full capacity, trade sources said.
Last week, refining margins in Rotterdam reached their highest levels in seven months, according to Reuters data using standard product yields.
A couple of unsold June Oseberg and Ekofisk cargoes were still available, helping to neutralise reports of delayed June Forties loadings, traders said.
The market was still waiting to see the July loading programmes for the Forties, Ekofisk and Flotta export systems.
